headline: Parks Canada Discovery Pass and Camping Requirements
reservation: Entry requires a valid Parks Canada Discovery Pass or daily admission fee, which can be obtained at the visitor centre. Camping reservations are managed through the national booking service; check the official Parks Canada site for current seasonal opening dates and site availability.

days.title: Dunes and Acadian Shorelines

stops.name: Kellys Beach Boardwalk
stops.detail: Cross the salt marshes on a long boardwalk to reach the protected sand dunes and the Northumberland Strait.

stops.name: Callanders Beach
stops.detail: Explore the tidal flats and calm lagoons, which are ideal for observing shorebirds at low tide.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes from the gateway; internal park roads are well-maintained.
days.note: Boardwalks may be slippery in morning mist; stay on marked paths to protect sensitive dune grass.

days.title: River Valleys and Forested Trails

stops.name: Kouchibouguac River Trail
stops.detail: Follow the winding river through mixed wood forests, looking for local wildlife and peaceful water views.

stops.name: Bog Trail
stops.detail: Walk the specialized boardwalk over a peat bog to see carnivorous plants and unique wetland vegetation.

days.driving: Allow 75-90 minutes from Moncton; conditions vary with weather.
days.note: Biking is a popular way to traverse the extensive trail network; check local rentals in the park.

days.title: Mi'kmaq Heritage and Estuaries
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from the Visitor Centre

stops.name: Wigwam Point
stops.detail: Visit this historic site to learn about the indigenous Mi'kmaq connection to the land and water.

stops.name: Claire-Fontaine Trail
stops.detail: Hike through abandoned orchard lands and forest to reach scenic vistas of the St. Louis Lagoon.

days.driving: Daily travel within the park is minimal, typically under 30 minutes between trailheads.
days.note: Black flies and mosquitoes are prevalent in June; consider timing your visits to breezy coastal areas.

intel.title: Beach Access
intel.text: Kellys Beach is the most popular destination; the main lot may reach capacity by midday in July. Use the overflow areas or cycle from the South Kouchibouguac campground.

intel.title: Network Coverage
intel.text: Signal is reliable near the Visitor Centre and Highway 11 but degrades quickly in the deep forest trails. Offline navigation is recommended for the northern sections of the park.

intel.title: Gateway Services
intel.text: Full services including fuel and groceries are available in Saint-Louis-de-Kent and Richibucto. There are no fueling stations located within the national park boundaries.

intel.title: Tidal Fluctuations
intel.text: Access to certain sandbars and lagoon views changes with the tide. Check the daily tide tables posted at the Visitor Centre to plan your beach walks.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: Secondary park roads may remain closed until late May depending on snowmelt. Check the official Parks Canada 'Facilities and Services' page for current status.

plan.arrival: Arrive via Moncton (YQM), pick up a rental vehicle, and head north on Highway 11. Stop in Richibucto for regional Acadian supplies before entering the park.
plan.vehicle: The park is highly accessible for RVs and standard cars alike; most major roads and parking lots are paved.
plan.goldenHour: Kellys Beach Boardwalk for sunrise over the Northumberland Strait; check seasonal times.
